items.title: Slow and extremely high memory usage (>10GB)
items.body:
Just download and install the shotcut-win64-200412.exe and use on a very small clip (50MB .mkv, 6 min, 1080 screen captured from OBS) to add subtitle. The computer is the Lenovo T490, 24GB memory, 1 TB NVME drive and Intel i7 CPU, 4 cores/8 threads with Win10. CPU usage is about 12~20% throughout.

New to this, not sure what's the right way to do it properly, so I break up the clip into ~ 40 fragments and half of the fragments with a Text_simple filter for the subtitle. The more fragments it has the slower it became and higher memory usage will be. Eventually it consumes > 13GB. It is extremely slow with the high amount of memory usage(like over 3 GB) that every action(like select a segment in the timeline, add a new text filter, save project, export video) will take over an hour or 2 to respond. Also noticed the list of filters failed to scroll properly.  Arrow key does not work. It does scroll when using the scroll bar, but all entries are from the filters in the 1st page.

The workaround is to save/close it when it's over 4GB memory and restart/reload the app/project. After the reload, the memory usage is about 3.5GB. Any action(break up fragment, add new filter, copy/paste filter) performs after that will increase the amount of memory usage a lot, in GB. Perform couple actions and then save/restart the app, process repeat. Shouldn't be too difficult to reproduce the problem, but let me know if you fail to reproduce.

items.title: Nearly one second is frozen after a cut
items.body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Download this 18-second video - https://uloz.to/file/DRkfa60ecVdz/aircraft-mts . Play the video on your computer, it should play smooth.
2. Open a new project in Shotcut, leave video mode on automatic, no proxy.
3. Import the aircraft.mts into the Playlist
4. In the Source player set the IN point to 15:10 and leave the OUT point at 18:10 (that makes a 3 sec clip)
5. Put this 3-sec clip TWO times on the timeline so that we have one cut (that will be enough for our need)
Your Shotcut should look like this now:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9153595/102723695-0ce4fe80-430a-11eb-9084-dcc2cfd03d29.png)

6. Now play the video on the Timeline and focus on the cut between these two clips - **right after the cut the video is frozen for about one second**.
7. Export the video to MJPEG - the same is in the exported file.

---
Windows 10 Pro, version 2004
Shotcut 20.11.28

items.title: converting a clip with detached audio makes the clip black on the timeline
items.body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Download this 18-second video - https://uloz.to/file/DRkfa60ecVdz/aircraft-mts . 
2. Open a new project in Shotcut, leave video mode on automatic, no proxy.
3. Drag the downloaded `aircraft.MTS` directly to the timeline.
4. Right click the clip on the Timeline -> click `More` -> `Detach audio`. Shotcut creates an A1 audio track and puts the detached audio in it.
5. In the Properties tab, click `Convert` button to get the "Convert to Edit-friendly" dialogue, leave the "Better" option and save the converted clip. Shotcut creates `aircraft - Converted.mov` and replaces the original clip on the timeline with the new one.
6. Play the timeline. The video is black now.
7. The same behavior occurs with an MP4 from different camera brand.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9153595/102775740-b91bf900-438d-11eb-87eb-1f98e9b16d6b.png)


---
Windows 10 Pro, version 2004
Shotcut 20.11.28
